The reason 1.9 feels scary is you're staring at the wrong number. ROAS is revenue ÷ spend — it doesn't know your margin is a healthy 60% or that your real cost to land a customer is only ₹809. A 1.9 ROAS on a 30%-margin brand would be a problem; on yours it's fine.

That gap is the whole story. When clicks are healthy but conversion sits under 1%, you're not failing to grab attention — you're grabbing the wrong attention. The proof is the 0.81% itself. If this were a creative or CTR problem, clicks would be scarce. Instead clicks are abundant and purchases are rare — that's an intent mismatch, not an attention one.

The lever: stop optimising for clicks and tighten toward intent. Layer in high-intent signals — retargeting cart/viewers, lookalikes off actual purchasers, and on the Google side, branded and category search keywords with a negative list to kill junk queries.
